description: Countertops data — Granite vs Quartz comparison

graniteVsQuartz.title: Granite vs Quartz Countertops
graniteVsQuartz.summary: Choose quartz if budget permits (nearly double the cost of granite) and only from reputed brands. For investment projects, granite is cost-effective, durable, and works just as well.

granite.label: Granite

properties.porosity: Porous material — absorbs liquids slowly if sealer is not applied
properties.colorRange: Commonly used in darker colours, especially black, as it hides stains better
properties.bestFor: Indian households due to heavy cooking and spice usage
properties.appearance: Natural stone patterns — unique variations in each slab

idealFor: Traditional Indian cooking with heavy spices and oils
Those who prefer darker kitchen aesthetics
granite.verdict: Best for: investment/rental projects — cost-effective, durable, and works just as well.

quartz.label: Quartz

properties.porosity: Non-porous in good-quality brands; does not absorb liquids
properties.colorRange: Available in a wide range of colours and patterns
properties.maintenance: Lighter shades require regular cleaning to maintain appearance
properties.cost: Nearly double the cost of granite
properties.durability: Durable but only from reputed brands
properties.appearance: Consistent patterns and colours — engineered uniformity

idealFor: Those willing to invest in reputed brands only
quartz.criticalCondition: Must be from reputed brands — low-quality quartz can absorb liquids despite being marketed as non-porous
quartz.verdict: Best for: personal homes with adequate budget — but ONLY from reputed brands.

decisionMatrix.reason: More economical, durable, and tenants won't value the premium of quartz
Cost-effective without significant compromise; choose darker colours for stain hiding
Wider aesthetic options, non-porous (with good brands), modern look
Black/dark granite hides stains from turmeric, oil, and spices better than light quartz
Consistent patterns and wide colour range suit themed designs

graniteVsQuartz.keyFact: Quartz costs nearly double that of granite. Low-quality quartz CAN absorb liquids despite marketing claims. Always insist on reputed quartz brands.
graniteVsQuartz.takeaway: Choose quartz if budget permits (nearly double the cost of granite) and only from reputed brands, as low-quality quartz can absorb liquids. Best for personal use. For investment projects, granite is cost-effective, durable, and works just as well.
